items.author: Mattertrades
items.context: Matter (en inglés): analiza el hackeo de $6.400M a Binance. Binance cubrió a los clientes con ~$5.000M de activos propios, así que casi no hubo compras en el mercado y el BTC robado sigue en manos del atacante. Su tesis es que tras el hackeo los desks bajaron sus saldos en exchanges, hubo menos liquidez para absorber liquidaciones y por eso un problema de custodia sigue apareciendo en el gráfico de BTC (~$2,71T a ~$2,15T de capitalización cripto). Cuenta mediana, post de hace ~30 min con 5 guardados y 1 respuesta.
items.suggested_text:
The part that gets lost in "customers were made whole" is what that guarantee actually is: a claim on the exchange's balance sheet, not a key you hold. It worked this time because Binance had roughly $5B of the exact assets on hand. And the mechanism you describe cuts both ways: when desks pull size off exchanges after a hack, liquidity thins for everyone, but whoever already held $BTC in self-custody was never in the queue waiting to be covered.

Self-custody doesn't remove risk, it changes its shape. Counterparty and freeze risk go away; backup, inheritance and supply-chain risk become yours to design around. That trade-off is what I wrote about here: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

A treasury can replace coins one for one. What it can't replace is the assumption that the coins were ever yours while they sat there.
